text:
Alex Ng: quick heads up — I hit a regression in continuous batch formation on r-infer-prod-3. When kernel selection falls back to fp32 the KV cache memory jumps ~1.2GB in <200ms and we see transient OOMs / batch drops.

Maria Lopez: do you have the profile/flamegraph link?

Alex Ng: uploaded a short GPU mem timeline + perf profile to the perf bucket. TL;DR: FP32 kernel increases per-token KV footprint by ~5x (estimates from model X: 24KB -> 120KB per token). With typical queue depth >12 we cross eviction watermark and trigger aggressive eviction -> lots of dropped batches.

Chen Wang: can you paste the numbers? p50/p95/p99 latency shift?

Alex Ng: sure — p50/p95 similar, p99 latency spikes x3 during the drops window. Eviction rate went from ~18% baseline to 61% during the incident window. Also saw kernel_selection.switches count spike.

Priya Patel: sounds like kernel selection scoring ignores KV memory delta. I'd like to propose: 1) factor kernel_memory_delta into kernel score; 2) compute a dynamic token_budget that uses the worst-case per-token KV footprint for the kernel we might fall back to; 3) enforce a per-device kv_reserved_pct so we never eat the entire cache.

Maria Lopez: +1. can you sketch a config so we have something concrete to iterate on? Also we'll need perf tests for synthetic sequences.

Alex Ng: sketch below — this is intentionally conservative.

```
{
  "batching": {
    "min_tokens": 4,
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "target_token_budget": "dynamic",
    "token_budget_policy": "kv-aware",
    "kv_reserved_pct": 20
  },
  "kernel_selection": {
    "preference": ["int8","fp16","fp32"],
    "memory_penalty_coeff": 0.8,
    "fallback_threshold_bytes": 200000000
  }
}
```

Chen Wang: how do you compute the dynamic token_budget? formula?

Alex Ng: token_budget = floor((free_cache_bytes - safety_margin) / per_token_kv_footprint_estimate). per_token estimate is derived per-model-per-kernel from nightly profiling. safety_margin = max(64MB, 5% of total_cache) to cover eviction jitter.

Priya Patel: we should add a short-circuit: if kernel_fallback_likelihood > 30% (based on sequence length heuristics and kernel saturation signals), enforce an even smaller token_budget or throttle admissions for that queue for 30s.

Maria Lopez: :thumbsup: Also add a canary test — 10k synthetic requests with mixed seq lengths and a small TTL for cache to exercise eviction behavior. If eviction rate exceeds 40% we fail the canary.

Alex Ng: will create a PR with feature flagging and a canary job. Also adding tracing for kernel_choice and per_token_kv_bytes. Quick admission pseudocode I'm going to add to the runtime: 

```
# admission pseudocode
if kernel_predicted_memory_delta > fallback_threshold_bytes:
    reduce_token_budget = ceil(kernel_predicted_memory_delta / per_token_est)
    batch.token_budget = max(min_tokens, batch.token_budget - reduce_token_budget)
    queue.mark_preemptible(True)
    log("kv_aware_admission", kernel=chosen_kernel, delta=kernel_predicted_memory_delta, new_budget=batch.token_budget)
```

Chen Wang: another mitigation: if we detect repeated fp32 fallbacks on a device, temporarily cap batch token count to 4 and disable aggressive coalescing for 30s to let cache settle. Could avoid multiple eviction storms.

Priya Patel: agree. Also we should capture kernel_choice histogram in traces and include per-token-kv bytes so we can automatically compute a rolling per-kernel per-model footprint estimate.

DeployBot: New canary job queued: canary/kv-aware-batcher-20240326-1. Status: queued.

Alex Ng: plan — PR with flags today, canary run tomorrow. If canary eviction_rate > 40% or p99 latency regresses > 2x we will rollback. Assigning to @Maria and @Priya for review.

Maria Lopez: thanks Alex. assign to Alex + Priya. Ping me when canary is up and link the perf artifacts so SRE can look at scale implications.

Priya Patel: I'll add the tracing bits and a small offline job to compute per-token_kv_estimates nightly.

Alex Ng: cool. I'll include a small synthetic generator that simulates long-tails and short requests so we can measure fallback likelihood. Will post PR link here in ~3h. :thinking:
